key_insight: GS-BMT establishes a large donor–recipient genomic research platform for blood and marrow transplantation, rather than an AI drug-discovery study.
clinical_relevance: The initiative aims to improve transplant risk prediction and donor selection, but the reported analyses do not establish clinical utility.
method: Genome-wide SNP genotyping of 30,718 donor–recipient pairs, with sequencing and methylation profiling in selected subsets.
Compared Cox, random survival forest, and deep neural network survival models in 9,262 patients with acute myeloid leukemia.
Assessed inherited susceptibility to clonal hematopoiesis using polygenic scores in 19,750 donors.
evidence_signal: Clinical-variable survival models showed similarly modest discrimination (C-index: 0.63, 0.62, 0.62), while donor polygenic scores differed slightly by relatedness but not age.
watch_item: The polygenic-score risk scenarios were illustrative assumptions, not demonstrated clinical risk estimates, and require outcome validation before informing donor selection.
paper_title: Genomic Studies in Blood and Marrow Transplantation (GS-BMT): An NCI-CIBMTR genomic medicine initiative in hematopoietic cell transplantation
